title: Scaled content abuse
content: Scaled content abuse is Google’s policy term for generating many pages primarily to manipulate rankings rather than help users.

meta.why: A glossary needs useful explanations, and repeating the same shallow entry across many keyword variations gives readers nothing new.
meta.example: A site creates near-identical definition pages with only a location or adjective changed.
meta.check: Keep minor variants together, and create a separate page only when it serves a distinct reader need with enough useful material.
meta.limitation: The policy looks at the purpose and value of the pages, whoever or whatever produced the text.
meta.sources: Google Search Central: scaled content abuse | https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies#scaled-content | Platform documentation
